# MCP tools reference

Tools exposed by the WeRForces MCP server (`/mcp` or `dist/mcp/stdio.js`). See [Tutorial 5](../tutorials/05-ai-agents-with-mcp.md) for setup.

Instructions sent to the client when it connects:

> WeRForces is a computer-generated forces (CGF) military simulation.
> Start with get_situation to learn the scenario, forces, terrain size and town names.
> Positions are local metres (x east, y north, from the south-west corner) or {lat,lon} or {town:"Name"}.
> Forces: 1 = Blue, 2 = Red, 3 = Neutral. Entities can be grouped into units (ids U..); task a unit to move it in formation.
> Use list_catalog for entity type and unit template ids. Use advance_time to simulate while paused and get a summary of what happened.

## `get_situation` _(read-only)_

Overview of the simulation: scenario, time, running state, strength per force, terrain size and towns, units and tactical graphics. Call this first.

No parameters.

## `list_entities` _(read-only)_

List entities with position, damage and current activity. Filter by force, domain or unit.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force` | `1` or `2` or `3` or `0` |  | 1 Blue, 2 Red, 3 Neutral, 0 Other |
| `domain` | `"ground"` \| `"lifeform"` \| `"air"` \| `"surface"` |  |  |
| `unitId` | string |  |  |
| `aliveOnly` | boolean |  | exclude destroyed entities |

## `get_entity` _(read-only)_

Full details of one entity: kinematics, damage, ROE, task/plan, ammunition and current sensor contacts.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |

## `explain` _(read-only)_

Why an entity or unit is or is not moving, shooting or seeing the enemy: blockers (no line of sight and what blocks it, out of range, ROE, out of ammo or fuel, pinned, halted on contact, broken, order still on its way...) with suggested fixes. Use it whenever something does not do what you ordered.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | Entity or unit id |

## `give_order`

Give an order in plain words, the way a commander would say it: "<who> <verb> <where/what> [modifiers]". Who: unit or entity names (join several with "and"). Verbs: move to (covered, fast, slowly, at N km/h), attack, follow, defend/overwatch/screen <place> [facing <direction>] [width <m>], ambush <area> [from <place>], search <area>, patrol <route>, follow route <route>, fire [N rounds] on <place>, smoke <place>, orbit <place> [radius N km], mount <carrier>, dismount, resupply [from X], breach <minefield>, wait N min, stop, hold fire, return fire, fire at will. Places: town or graphic names, objects, "x y", or "2 km north of Brenham". Use dryRun to check how it is understood. Prefer this for simple orders; use assign_task for details it cannot express.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | string | yes | The order, e.g. "Team ARMOR move to Calloway covered" |
| `dryRun` | boolean |  |  |

## `viewshed` _(read-only)_

What an entity (or a point) can see: the share of the ground within the radius that is in its line of sight, and the dead ground. Use it to choose observation posts, overwatch positions or covered approaches.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` | string or {x, y, height} | yes | entity id, or a position |
| `radius` | number |  |  |

## `set_sync_matrix`

Plan an operation in phases for a force (a synchronization matrix, or global plan). Each phase has a trigger and orders for units; phases start in order, each giving all its orders at once and announcing its name as a codeword (e.g. phase "Phase 2 Assault" sends codeword "PHASE 2 ASSAULT", which unit plans can wait for). Triggers: {type:"manual"} (start_phase), {type:"time",time} (s), {type:"codeword",codeword}, {type:"previousDone",delay?} (when the previous phase's orders are carried out), {type:"condition",ownerId,condition} (plan conditions). Orders: {targetId, text} with the order in words as for give_order without the name ("move to Calloway covered", "defend OBJ CALLOWAY facing north", "hold fire"), or {targetId, task}. An empty phases list removes the matrix.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force` | `"blue"` \| `"red"` \| `"neutral"` | yes |  |
| `phases` | array of {id, name, trigger, orders} | yes |  |

## `start_phase`

Start a phase of a synchronization matrix now, whatever its trigger.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `force` | `"blue"` \| `"red"` \| `"neutral"` | yes |  |
| `phaseId` | string | yes |  |

## `send_codeword`

Send a codeword to a force (players: their own). Plans waiting for it ({type:"codeword"} conditions) go on: use it to trigger phases ("EXECUTE", "PHASE 2"). Also lists codewords sent so far.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `codeword` | string | yes |  |
| `force` | `"blue"` \| `"red"` \| `"neutral"` |  | default blue (exercise control only) |

## `get_alerts`

The attention queue: what needs looking at now (units idle after finishing their orders, broken, out of fuel or ammunition, leader lost, losses, failed tasks, under fire, first contact), newest first. Pass acknowledge: true to clear them once handled.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `acknowledge` | boolean |  | Acknowledge all open alerts after reading them |

## `assign_task`

Give an entity or unit a task (replaces its current plan). moveTo/orbit/fireMission need `to`; followRoute/patrol need `routeId`; attack/follow need `targetEntityId`; mount needs `targetEntityId` (the carrier entity or unit); wait needs `duration`; dismount (for a carrier) needs nothing; breach (engineers) needs `graphicId` of a minefield or obstacle; resupply sends it to the nearest friendly supply vehicle (or `targetEntityId`) to refuel and rearm (helicopters land beside it). Tactical tasks: overwatch/defend/screen need `to` (the position) and take `facing` (degrees) and `width` (units deploy in a line); ambush also needs `graphicId` (the kill zone area) and opens fire only when an enemy enters it; screen falls back before an enemy gets within reach of its direct fire (at least 1.5 km) or as soon as it comes under fire; search needs `graphicId` (an area) and sweeps it. Holding still, infantry dig in and vehicles go hull-down. Set `smoke` on a fireMission for smoke rounds. fireMission is indirect fire by artillery or mortars on a location (`rounds` per tube, optional `radius` sheaf). Unmanned systems: strike (one-way attack drones: FPV, loitering munitions) needs `targetEntityId` and flies into it; loiter takes `graphicId` (an area it sweeps again and again) or `to` and `radius` (a point it circles), with `attack` to strike the first suitable enemy found and `prefer` (what to go for, best first: armored, light, soft, lifeform, artillery, air-defense…, "any"); swarmSearch (a unit of drones) needs `graphicId` and shares the area out, with `attack` each strikes a different target; swarmAttack (a unit of drones) takes `targetIds` or `graphicId` (an area) and spreads its members over distinct targets.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targetId` | string | yes | entity (E..) or unit (U..) id |
| `type` | `"moveTo"` \| `"followRoute"` \| `"patrol"` \| `"attack"` \| `"follow"` \| `"orbit"` \| `"wait"` \| `"fireMission"` \| `"mount"` \| `"dismount"` \| `"breach"` \| `"resupply"` \| `"overwatch"` \| `"defend"` \| `"screen"` \| `"ambush"` \| `"search"` \| `"strike"` \| `"loiter"` \| `"swarmSearch"` \| `"swarmAttack"` | yes |  |
| `to` | {x, y, lat, lon, town} |  | Location as {x,y}, {lat,lon} or {town} |
| `routeId` | string |  |  |
| `targetEntityId` | string |  |  |
| `duration` | number |  | seconds |
| `radius` | number |  | orbit radius in m (default 2000), or fire mission sheaf radius (default 0) |
| `rounds` | integer (1–100) |  | fire mission rounds per tube (default 3) |
| `smoke` | boolean |  | fire mission: smoke rounds instead of high explosive |
| `graphicId` | string |  | breach: the minefield or obstacle; ambush: the kill zone area; search, loiter, swarmSearch, swarmAttack: the area |
| `attack` | boolean |  | loiter, swarmSearch: attack suitable enemies found |
| `prefer` | array of string |  | loiter, swarmSearch, swarmAttack: what to go for, best first (armour classes, symbols, type ids, "any") |
| `targetIds` | array of string |  | swarmAttack: the targets to spread over |
| `facing` | number (0–360) |  | overwatch/defend/screen/ambush: direction to face, degrees from north |
| `width` | number |  | defend/screen/ambush: frontage in m for a unit |
| `speedKmh` | number |  |  |
| `covered` | boolean |  | moveTo: take a covered route, out of sight of known enemies' direct fire where possible |

## `assign_plan`

Give an entity or unit a plan: an ordered list of statements executed in sequence. Statement kinds: {kind:"task", task:{type:"moveTo",target:{town:"X"}}} (task types as in assign_task, with target/center positions), {kind:"setRoe", roe}, {kind:"setSpeed", speed (m/s)}, {kind:"setAltitude", altitude}, {kind:"setFormation", formation}, {kind:"setReactions", reactions:{onContact:"halt"|"continue", withdrawBelow:0..1, callForFire:true|false}}, {kind:"waitUntil", condition:{type:"simTime",time}|{type:"inArea",areaId}|{type:"enemyInArea",areaId}|{type:"enemyDetected"}|{type:"underFire"}|{type:"strengthBelow",fraction}|{type:"fuelBelow",fraction}|{type:"ammoBelow",fraction}|{type:"entityDestroyed",entityId}|{type:"codeword",codeword}|{type:"all"|"any",conditions:[...]}|{type:"not",condition}}, {kind:"if", condition, then:[statements], else:[statements]}, {kind:"while", condition, body:[statements]} (repeats while the condition holds), {kind:"sendCodeword", codeword} (plans of the same force waiting for it go on), {kind:"report", text} (a radio message). Codewords coordinate units: e.g. one unit sends "PHASE 2" when it reaches a phase line, others wait for it.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targetId` | string | yes |  |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `loop` | boolean |  |  |
| `statements` | array of object | yes |  |

## `embark`

Instantly put infantry (an entity or a whole unit) inside a carrier (an entity or a unit, whose seats are shared out), e.g. to set up a mechanized platoon with its squad mounted. Use assign_task type "mount" to make them walk to the carrier instead. With `dismount: true`, lets the passengers of the carrier(s) given in carrierId out now.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `passengerId` | string |  | infantry entity or unit id |
| `carrierId` | string | yes | carrier entity or unit id |
| `dismount` | boolean |  |  |

## `stop`

Stop an entity or unit (clears its task and plan).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targetId` | string | yes |  |

## `set_roe` _(idempotent)_

Set rules of engagement for an entity or unit: fireAtWill, returnFire or holdFire.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targetId` | string | yes |  |
| `roe` | `"fireAtWill"` \| `"returnFire"` \| `"holdFire"` | yes |  |

## `set_unit_superior` _(idempotent)_

Put a unit under a superior unit in the chain of command (or make it independent with superiorId null). An order given to the superior passes down to its subordinate units: moves keep their positions relative to each other, defend/overwatch/screen/ambush spread them in a line, other tasks go to all. With the orderDelay simulation rule on, each level adds a delay.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unitId` | string | yes |  |
| `superiorId` | string/null | yes |  |

## `aggregate_unit`

Switch a unit (and the units under it) between entity level and aggregate level. Aggregated, it is one object: its members leave the entity simulation, it moves at the speed of its slowest member type (move, follow route, wait, defend, overwatch and attack; other orders split it up first) and fights other aggregates with Lanchester attrition, losing specific members. It splits into its members by itself when enemy entities come close (see set_aggregation_policy). Use it for forces far from the action, to keep large scenarios fast. Returns the unit with its aggregate strength.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unitId` | string | yes |  |
| `aggregate` | boolean | yes | true: aggregate; false: split back into entities (in formation, with their own damage, ammunition and fuel) |

## `set_aggregation_policy` _(idempotent)_

When aggregated units split up and join up again. Defaults: an aggregate disaggregates when an enemy entity comes within 3000 m; a unit that split up by itself aggregates again once no enemy entity has been within 5000 m for 120 s. Fields left out keep their values; returns the policy.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `autoDisaggregate` | boolean |  |  |
| `disaggregateRange` | number (100–50000) |  | metres |
| `autoReaggregate` | boolean |  |  |
| `reaggregateRange` | number (100–100000) |  | metres, at least disaggregateRange |
| `reaggregateDelay` | number (0–86400) |  | seconds |

## `set_simulation_rules` _(idempotent)_

Turn optional parts of the model on or off for this scenario. Suppression (fire pins and degrades the target), morale (units become shaken and break under losses) and fuel (vehicles and aircraft burn fuel) are on by default; orderDelay (orders take 5-60 s to pass down the chain of command, by echelon) is off by default. Useful for comparison runs.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `suppression` | boolean |  |  |
| `morale` | boolean |  |  |
| `fuel` | boolean |  |  |
| `orderDelay` | boolean |  |  |

## `edit_catalog`

Add or change a catalog entry for this scenario (entity type, weapon, sensor or unit template), e.g. a new vehicle variant: start from list_catalog's fields of a similar entry, change what differs, give it a new id. Fields are checked; new entities use it at once. remove: true deletes a custom entry.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `section` | `"entity-types"` \| `"weapons"` \| `"sensors"` \| `"unit-templates"` | yes |  |
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `entry` | object |  |  |
| `remove` | boolean |  |  |

## `set_jamming`

Switch a jammer (an electronic warfare entity, e.g. R-330Zh Zhitel, Krasukha-2, Stryker MFEW) on or off. While on, enemy radios within its range are jammed: orders to them arrive a minute late, they do not share contacts within their unit, cannot call for fire and do not hear codewords; radar jammers cut enemy radars' range.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes |  |
| `on` | boolean | yes |  |

## `set_drone_control`

Unmanned systems (an entity, or every drone of a unit): assign the operator it is flown from (`controllerId`, a drone operator team or control station of its force; null: any of its force's), what it does when its datalink is lost (`lostLink`: hover, return to its operator, continue its task, land; null: its type's) and how much it does without a link (`autonomy`: remote, supervised, autonomous; null: its type's). An entity's `link` shows whether its datalink is up and why not (jammed, out of range, no line of sight, no operator, fibre run out).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | yes | entity (E..) or unit (U..) id |
| `controllerId` | string/null |  |  |
| `lostLink` | `"hover"` \| `"return"` \| `"continue"` \| `"land"` or null |  |  |
| `autonomy` | `"remote"` \| `"supervised"` \| `"autonomous"` or null |  |  |

## `quick_battle`

Replace the scenario with a generated, ready-to-run battle: pick the mission (from Blue's side), each force's nation, composition, size and support, time and weather. Both forces are placed on land either side of an objective (a town near the middle when there is one), with the mission's graphics and a synchronization matrix per force; start the simulation to fight it. Returns the mission brief.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mission` | `"meeting"` \| `"attack"` \| `"defend"` \| `"delay"` \| `"recon"` |  | default attack |
| `blue` | {nation, composition, size, support} |  |  |
| `red` | {nation, composition, size, support} |  |  |
| `time` | number (0–24) |  | local time at the start, hours (default 10) |
| `weather` | `"clear"` \| `"haze"` \| `"fog"` \| `"rain"` |  |  |
| `distance` | number (1000–20000) |  | metres between the sides at the start |
| `civilians` | boolean |  |  |
| `seed` | integer (-9007199254740991–9007199254740991) |  | same seed and options, same battle |
| `name` | string |  |  |

## `set_pattern_of_life`

Fill the map with background civilians: cars driving between towns along the roads and people walking about the towns (neutral, force 3). They run from shots and blasts nearby; any killed are logged. Set both to 0 to remove them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vehicles` | integer (0–300) |  |  |
| `pedestrians` | integer (0–300) |  |  |

## `set_environment` _(idempotent)_

Set the time of day and weather. Darkness cuts the range of eyes and binoculars (night-vision goggles keep about 60%, thermal sights are unaffected); fog and precipitation cut every optical sensor; rain and snow slow movement off roads; wind drifts smoke. Fields left out keep their values. Returns the current environment (local time, sun altitude, light level).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | string |  | date at the scenario start |
| `time` | number (0–24) |  | local solar time at the scenario start, in hours (e.g. 4.5 = 04:30) |
| `visibility` | number (50–100000) |  | metres; fog is a few hundred, clear is 20000+ |
| `precipitation` | `"none"` \| `"rain"` \| `"heavyRain"` \| `"snow"` |  |  |
| `windSpeed` | number (0–40) |  | m/s |
| `windFrom` | number (0–360) |  | degrees the wind blows from |

## `set_reactions` _(idempotent)_

Automatic behaviours that run alongside tasks: onContact "halt" makes the entity/unit stop and fight while a hostile is within weapon range, then resume its task; withdrawBelow (0-1) makes a unit abandon its plan and fall back (to withdrawTo, default its current position) when its strength drops below that fraction, or an entity when its weapons are knocked out; callForFire makes it request fire missions from idle friendly artillery in range on hostiles it sees (not within 150 m of friendly troops).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targetId` | string | yes |  |
| `onContact` | `"continue"` \| `"halt"` |  |  |
| `withdrawBelow` | number (0–1) |  |  |
| `withdrawTo` | {x, y, lat, lon, town} |  | Location as {x,y}, {lat,lon} or {town} |
| `callForFire` | boolean |  |  |

## `run_batch`

Monte Carlo analysis: replicate a scenario (a stored one by name, or the current state) with different random seeds and summarise the outcomes: losses per force (mean, standard deviation, 95% confidence interval, histogram), loss exchange ratio, which force holds each area at the end, rounds fired. Runs in the background on the server; waits up to `waitSeconds` for the result, else returns the job id to check with jobId.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `scenario` | string |  | stored scenario name (default: the current state) |
| `runs` | integer (1–1000) |  | replications (default 10) |
| `durationMinutes` | number |  | simulated minutes per run (default 30) |
| `seed` | integer (-9007199254740991–9007199254740991) |  |  |
| `waitSeconds` | number (0–600) |  | how long to wait for the result (default 120) |
| `jobId` | string |  | check on a batch started earlier instead of starting one |

## `after_action_report` _(read-only)_

After-action review of the run so far (or of a loaded recording): strength and losses per force, every kill with killer, weapon and time, rounds fired per weapon, bookmarks.

No parameters.

## `replay_state` _(read-only)_

Where everything was at a past simulation time, from the recording: entity positions (grid, lat/lon), damage and units.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |

| `time` | number | yes | simulation time in seconds |
| `force` | integer (0–3) |  |  |
